image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on dry, textured ground. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a grey body with brown chest markings, and orange legs. The background consists of blurred earth and sparse vegetation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a yellowish-green hue typical of a mallard drake.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and compact. The plumage texture appears dense and smooth, indicative of waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible leg is orange and positioned towards the rear of the body. While the webbing detail is slightly obscured by the angle and resolution, the general structure and color are correct for a duck.
The folded wing is visible on the side, showing the correct placement and feather layering. The speculum (blue patch) is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail area shows the characteristic upward curl of the central feathers typical of male mallards.
